title: Create a responsive old book exchange activity page
goal: makes the area of ​​the active page clear and adapts to mobile phones and wider screens.
summary: uses header, nav, main, section and footer to describe the page structure. First use the narrow screen style to maintain a clear reading order, and then use media queries to switch the navigation and content arrangement in the wide screen.
tasks: Change .site-header, .site-nav, .reading-content and .site-footer into corresponding semantic tags in index.html. Add aria-label="in-page navigation" to nav.
Change #schedule and #visit to two sections within main, retaining the title, existing class name, and target of the navigation link.

Add a media query for a minimum width of 680px in style.css. On the wide screen, the event name and navigation are placed side by side, and event arrangements and arrival methods are arranged in two equal-width columns.

Check the preview narrower than 680px, the navigation area is arranged below the site name, and the two blocks of text are also arranged one above the other. Click the navigation link to confirm that you can locate the corresponding content.

example.note: photography sharing page first displays two pieces of content in a single column. At 720px width, photo descriptions and shooting parameters can be read side by side.

hint: If there are two columns in a narrow screen, first check whether the two-column rule is written in the min-width media query. In-page links also require that the fragment in the href corresponds to the section id.
